newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FENERBAHCE HOPE TO HAVE NEW COACH AT HELM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FENERBAHCE HOPE TO HAVE NEW COACH AT HELM.

text.p: Fenerbahce, who took the drastic step of sacking their Brazilian coach Sebastiao Lazaroni on Thursday, hope to have Yugoslav Todor Veselinovic at the helm for their crucial league clash with Istanbul rivals Galatasaray on Sunday.
Fenerbahce expect to sign Veselinovic, who coached the team in the 1988-89 season, in time for Sunday's match. Veselinovic was due to arrive around midday on Friday for the signing.
Lazaroni's sacking follows a 2-1 defeat by Beskitas on Wednesday. Besiktas were playing with 10 men.
''There is no logical explanation for the fall of the team,'' said club deputy chairman Vefa Kucuk. ''As executives we are doing all we can. Lazaroni's mistakes are taking us away from our targets.''

Both Galatasaray and Fenerbahce are in dismal form, with neither recording a win since the season moved into its second phase. Fenerbahce, beaten last week by lowly Altay, have scored just two goals in league matches and Galatasaray one while Galatasaray have also been knocked out of the Turkish Cup.
Galatasaray coach Fatih Terim said Fenerbahce would be more dangerous following the Cup defeat and the sacking.
"Whatever happens, Fenerbahce will do its absolute best now. Now, like us, they only have one aim -- the league championship. Because of this, the match on Sunday will be very tough," Terim said.
Galatasaray lead the Turkish leage with 47 points, with Fenerbahce three points behind. Besiktas and Trabzonspor are in third and fourth positions, both on 42 points.

Galatasaray have followed Fenerbahce's lead in treating the build-up to Sunday's game as if it were a Cup final, banning the players from leaving the camp or receiving visitors until they travel to the ground for the match. The players have been told to keep their mobile telephone conversations to a minimum.
Terim's main concern is leading marksman Hakan Sukur's lack of goals. He was last on target in the week before the mid-season break with a hat-trick against Bursaspor.
Fenerbahce have an impressive home record and will enjoy a psychological advantage after their 4-0 trouncing of Galatasaray in October.
They will be hampered by minor injuries to Bosnian striker Elvir Bolic, defender Ilker Yagcioglu and midfielder Erol Bulut, who are, however, all likely to play on Sunday.
Fenerbahce - Fevzi Layic, Ilker Yagcioglu, Uche Okechukwu, Jes Hogh, Erol Bulut, Selahattin Ozbir, Mustafa Dogan, Augustine "Jay Jay" Okocha, Tayfun Korkut, Elvir Bolic, Saffet Sancakli.
Galatasaray - Mehmet Sen, Bulent Korkmaz, Feti Okuroglu, Vedat Inceefe, Iulian Filipescu, Suat Kaya, Tugay Kerimoglu, Georgi Hagi, Ergun Pembe, Hakan Sukur.
